Dr. Amara Okafor pressed her gloved hand against the viewport and watched the red dust swirl across the landscape. After seven months in transit and a harrowing descent, she was finally standing on Mars. Behind her, the rest of the crew bustled about, unpacking supplies and running system checks, but for a moment she allowed herself to simply look.

The horizon stretched out in shades of rust and ochre, broken only by the distant silhouette of Olympus Mons. It was silent, vast, and utterly unlike anything she had known on Earth. She felt both tiny and impossibly lucky.

"Okafor, we need you at the habitat controls," called Commander Reyes over the comm.

She took one last look at the alien sunrise and turned away from the window. There was much to do. The first day of a new world was only the beginning, and the colony would need every one of them to survive. Still, as she walked down the corridor, she could not stop smiling.
